raw_case_text:
A five-year-old male non-Caucasian patient presented with fever, myalgia, headache, and conjunctivitis for 5 days. His past medical history was unremarkable, with normal psychomotor development, no family history neurological diseases and no consanguinity. The patient was born and lived in Ceara, northeast Brazil, and family reported no recent travels.
After 1 week he developed tonic-clonic seizures. Neurological examination was normal at this point. Complete blood count, liver functions and acute reactants were normal. Serologies for HSV-1, HSV-2, CMV, EBV, VZV, HIV, and toxoplasmosis were negative. Brain MRI was normal. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed 15 cells, protein 16.6 mg/dL and glucose 68 mg/dL. He was started on acyclovir and ceftriaxone.
Two weeks after seizure onset, he presented with dystonia (Video 1) and oromandibular dyskinesia. On physical examination the patient was awake, his speech output was decreased, pupils were normal. Cranial nerves examination was unremarkable. Muscle strength was symmetric and deep tendon reflexes were normoactive and symmetric. One week later he developed focal motor seizures followed by decreased level of consciousness, dysautonomia, and central apnea. EEG showed extreme delta brush and valproate and phenytoin were started. He also received methylprednisolone followed by intravenous immunoglobulin with seizure resolution and improvement of level of consciousness, dysautonomia and orofacial dyskinesias within 2 weeks.
Anti-NMDAR antibodies were detected in serum (titer 1:25600) and CSF (titer 1:1024) after 3 weeks of symptom onset using tissue and cell-based assays as previously reported. CHIK serology was positive for both IgM and IgG, suggesting a recent infection. Dengue and Zika serologies were negative. CSF PCR for herpes viruses and arboviruses (CHIK, Dengue and Zika) were negative. Whole body CT and testis ultrasound were normal. Because of partial improvement (persistence of orofacial dyskinesias and impaired speech), the patient received rituximab and cyclophosphamide with good response. After 8 months he is seizure-free and has returned to school with only mild restlessness and inattention. Figure 1 describes the timeline of clinical features, investigation and treatment of the case report.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 5-year-old male presented with fever, myalgia, headache, and conjunctivitis for 5 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 5-year-old boy presented with fever, myalgia, headache, and conjunctivitis lasting 5 days. One week later, he developed tonic-clonic seizures. Two weeks following seizure onset, he developed dystonia and oromandibular dyskinesias with decreased speech output. One week later, he progressed to focal motor seizures, decreased level of consciousness, dysautonomia, and central apnea.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable; normal psychomotor development; no consanguinity or family history of neurological disease. Born and resident of Ceara, northeast Brazil; no recent travel.
subjective.review_of_systems: Decreased speech output, myalgia, headache. Home medications and allergies: None reported.

objective.physical_examination: Initial neurological exam normal. Follow-up exam: Awake with reduced speech output; normal pupils; unremarkable cranial nerve exam; symmetric muscle strength; normoactive, symmetric deep tendon reflexes; dystonia and oromandibular dyskinesia present. Subsequent deterioration revealed depressed level of consciousness, dysautonomia, and central apnea.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count, liver function tests, and acute phase reactants: normal. Serologies for HSV-1, HSV-2, CMV, EBV, VZV, HIV, and toxoplasmosis: negative. Testicular ultrasound: normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI: Normal. Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis: 15 cells/microL, protein 16.6 mg/dL, glucose 68 mg/dL. Whole-body CT: Normal (no teratoma/neoplasm). Electroencephalogram (EEG): Extreme delta brush pattern. CSF PCR for herpesviruses (HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV, CMV, EBV): negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis triggered by recent Chikungunya infection; anti-NMDAR antibodies detected in serum (titer 1:25,600) and CSF (titer 1:1,024). Chikungunya serology was positive for both IgM and IgG; Dengue and Zika serologies were negative. CSF PCR for neurotropic arboviruses (Chikungunya, Dengue, and Zika) was negative. Management and course: Initially started on empiric ceftriaxone and acyclovir; anticonvulsants (valproate and phenytoin) administered for seizures. Immunotherapy with pulse methylprednisolone followed by IVIG led to seizure control and resolution of apnea/dysautonomia. Due to residual dyskinesias and speech impairment, second-line immunotherapy with rituximab and cyclophosphamide was administered. At 8-month follow-up, the patient was seizure-free and attending school with only mild restlessness and inattention.
